title: Health Promotion

sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Compare two ways of helping someone get somewhere. You can drive them there yourself, which solves today's trip and nothing else. Or you can give them a bike, a helmet, a safe route, and enough practice to ride it, which changes where they can go for years. Health promotion is the second kind of help. The official wording says enabling people to increase control over their health, and control is the giveaway word: the point is not that a professional fixes you, it is that you end up with more say over how healthy you get to be.

### Question 2

Any serious improvement effort needs a scoreboard: specific numbers, a starting value, and a target date. Healthy People 2030 is that scoreboard for the whole country. It states where the nation stands now on things like tobacco use, childhood vaccination, and safe places to walk, and what number it is aiming for by 2030. Notice what a scoreboard does not do. It does not hand out licenses, pay anyone's hospital bill, or force a clinic to practice a certain way. Its power is that everyone is aiming at the same clearly stated numbers and can check whether the effort is working.

### Question 3

Health literacy is not a reading test, and that is the whole point of the current definition. Consider a map to somewhere you need to go. It is not enough to own the map, and not even enough to understand the symbols on it. You have to actually walk the route. That final step, doing something with the information, is why the word use was added. There is also a partner idea worth holding onto: organizational health literacy asks whether the people who drew the map made one an ordinary person could follow. Both halves matter, but only the first describes the individual.

### Question 4

Picture a soccer team. The goalkeeper has one job: stop the ball from entering this particular net. That is disease prevention, aimed squarely at a specific bad outcome. The strength and conditioning coach is not blocking any single shot; she is making the whole team faster, stronger, and better rested so they play well all season. That is health promotion, aimed at a better overall state. A good club employs both, and the two often use the same gym. What separates them is not who they serve or where they work, it is the direction they are aiming.

### Question 5

Suppose you genuinely want the ice cream and know exactly how good it is, but the only shop sits across a six-lane road with no crosswalk. Nothing is wrong with your motivation. What is missing is a safe way to get there. That obstacle is what behavior theorists call a barrier, and the Health Belief Model says people are constantly weighing the payoff of an action against its cost, hassle, and danger. When the cost side wins, no amount of extra persuading changes the outcome. The useful diagnostic question is whether the person is unconvinced or simply blocked, because the fixes are completely different.

### Question 6

Two people stand at the edge of the deep end, and both can describe the mechanics of swimming perfectly. One has practiced in the shallow end and thinks, I can do this. The other does not. Predict which one gets in the water, and more importantly, which one climbs back in after a bad mouthful. That specific belief, I can do this particular thing in this particular situation, is self-efficacy, and it is separate from knowing facts. It is built mainly by doing something successfully, which is why well-designed programs get you a small real win early instead of handing you a booklet.

### Question 7

Say the goal is that everyone at a school eats more fruit. Health education is the lesson and the poster explaining why fruit is worth eating. Health promotion includes that lesson, and also moves the fruit bowl to the front of the lunch line, writes fruit into the food service budget so it is reliably there, and gets the staff eating it in front of students. The lesson is one ingredient in a much larger recipe. Telling people what to do is the cheap part; arranging the surroundings so the healthy option is also the easy option is what makes the change hold.

### Question 8

Think of someone on a high diving board. Not walking to the pool at all is precontemplation. Standing at the end of the board looking down and genuinely arguing with yourself is contemplation. Curling your toes over the edge and counting is preparation. Being in the water is action. This client is on the board, deliberating, which is real movement and should be treated as progress. But nobody has jumped. Push a person who is still deliberating and they usually retreat down the ladder, so the productive move is to talk through what is keeping them up there rather than handing them a schedule.

### Question 9

To get children playing outside you can repeat the message endlessly, or you can build a safe, well-lit park two blocks away. The second works better because going outside stops being the brave choice and becomes the obvious one. That is what create supportive environments means: reshape the surroundings so healthy living is no longer uphill. It helps to learn all five Ottawa action areas as a set, because exam items usually put several of them side by side. The environment one is the one about sidewalks, lighting, safe workplaces, and physical space.

### Question 10

There is a real difference between a referee and a coach. The referee announces what is not allowed and enforces it; the moment she leaves, the rules stop operating. The coach asks what you want to get better at, demonstrates it, and has you practice until you can do it unsupervised; when he leaves, the ability stays with you. Note that a good lecture is neither, it is closer to handing someone a rulebook. Health promotion sides with the coach, because the goal is people who can steer their own health long after the nurse is out of the room.

### Question 11

Imagine a river people must cross daily. You can stand on the bank shouting swimming technique, or you can build a bridge. The shouting fades, and every person still fights the current alone every morning. The bridge simply works, for everyone, whether or not anyone is thinking about it. School meal standards and required activity time are the bridge: they change what happens by default, so the healthier outcome no longer depends on a fresh act of willpower. The general rule is that the further an intervention moves from asking individuals to decide, the more durable and far-reaching its effect tends to be.

### Question 12

Suppose you now know exactly how to bake bread. Useful, but you have no oven, no free hour in the day, and no one at home who notices whether bread appears. You will not bake. Knowing is only the first of three requirements. You also need the means, which planners call enabling factors, and something that rewards you for repeating it, which they call reinforcing factors. When a program fills people's heads and stops there, the evaluation shows exactly this signature: test scores climb, daily life is unchanged. The finding is not that education failed, it is that education alone was never sufficient.
